legend: Consider all divisors of some integer n%%ZSMJ0%%. Choose some of these divisors, then arrange them in a circle so that the ratio of any two adjacent numbers is a prime number.
Find the maximum number of divisors of n%%ZSMJ1%% you can choose, and find the appropriate arrangement.
input: The first line of input contains the integer n%%ZSMJ2%% (2≤n≤109%%ZSMJ3%%).
output: In the first line, print a single integer k%%ZSMJ4%% — the maximum number of divisors of n%%ZSMJ5%% you can choose.

In the second line, print k%%ZSMJ6%% integers — different divisors of n%%ZSMJ7%% in the order they appear on the circle. Any two adjacent and the first and last numbers in this list must differ by multiplication by some prime number.
